name: Huppim
overview: Huppim was a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, identified as a (grand?)son of Benjamin through Bela. He is mentioned among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, indicating his place in the early history of the Israelite people. Huppim is also associated with the group called the Huphamites, reflecting his tribal lineage within Benjamin.
namesAndTitles: The name Huppim means 'coast people,' which may reflect a geographical or cultural designation. He is also called Hupham in the Book of Numbers, though no specific meaning is given for this variant. Another related name, Huram, means '[my] brother is elevated,' highlighting a possible familial or honorific connection within the same genealogical line.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Huppim as a descendant of Benjamin and a son of Iri, with Maacah inferred as his brother. These relationships place him firmly within the Benjaminite lineage, connecting him to the broader family tree of Israel as recorded in the Chronicles and Genesis.
scriptureSignificance: Huppim's significance lies in his role as a member of the tribe of Benjamin during the patriarchal migration to Egypt, a foundational event in Israel's history. His mention among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt underscores his place in God's providential plan for the nation. The Huphamites, named after him, represent a distinct family group within Benjamin, preserving his legacy in the tribal structure of Israel.
